paras: The killing of Joseph Turner was the fatal shooting of a Memphis storekeeper by Deputy Sheriff Jim Reynolds at Turner's store on South Trezevant street in late June 1919. Reynolds had come with a white creditor, J. E. McCallum, to collect a debt; he was shot in the struggle and reportedly died the next day. The Chicago Defender carried the story on its front page and later reported a bystander's suit against the sheriff.

According to a Memphis dispatch dated June 27, McCallum was trying to collect a debt from Turner, whose store at 1257 South Trezevant street had earlier been closed by Squire McNamara. Turner had hired a lawyer and sought a court order; a later report traced the dispute to the serving of an attachment.

According to the Defender's correspondent, McCallum arrived with Reynolds and insulted and threatened Turner. Reynolds then drew his revolver, Turner seized it, and Reynolds was shot twice. The officer drew a second revolver and shot Turner dead; Arthur E. Ellison, who was in the store, later said Reynolds fired five times into Turner and sent the last bullet into Ellison's arm.

The first report said Reynolds might die, and a July 11 dispatch stated that he died the following day. Ellison, saying he took no part in the fight, filed suit in Circuit court against Sheriff Perry for $1,000. The first story ran under the headline "Warrants Issued," but its text named no warrant or arrest, and no inquest is reported.

The Chicago Defender was the only paper found to report the killing. Its front-page dispatch blamed "the uncouth method used by J. E. McCallum" in collecting the debt and identified both McCallum and Reynolds as white. Two weeks later it returned to the case only in a page-18 brief among lodge notices, reporting the lawsuit and the deputy's death without comment.
The first report did not say who shot Reynolds, while the July dispatch said he was "shot to the ground by Turner." The five-shot count comes from Ellison, who was suing the sheriff.

reader.title: Killing of Joseph Turner
bases: A white deputy sheriff accompanying a white creditor shot and killed Turner at his store in a dispute over a debt and the serving of an attachment; no mob or posse is described (A1, A2).

Turner was killed by a single deputy sheriff, with only the white creditor McCallum named as also present, during a struggle over the deputy's revolver while serving an attachment (A1, A2); no group of three or more and no mob action is reported.
Both reports appeared in one paper, the Chicago Defender, as separate Memphis dispatches (A1, A2); the later one rests on a bystander's lawsuit, and no other paper's account was found.
